description: a Rust multi-cloud storage pool daemon exposing an S3-compatible API over many provider accounts

authority.label: README.md (docs map, architecture at a glance, features)
AGENTS.md (deployment-config, docs-sync, issues & PRs, docs review gate)

axes.name: TERMINOLOGY
axes.detail: Does the change use this repo's vocabulary — backend, account, placement, tier, mount prefix, MVCC, vacuum, GC, sidecar, multipart, shard, bucket, key? Flag drift such as calling a backend a 'provider' inconsistently, a vacuum a 'cleanup', or placement a 'balancer'.

axes.name: DOC ALIGNMENT
axes.detail: AGENTS.md requires code and docs to move in the SAME commit, and names the owning doc for each area: README (features/docs map), docs/user-guide.md, docs/operator-guide.md, docs/cli-reference.md, docs/planning.md, docs/developer-guide.md, docs/architecture.md (including the test count, which must match `cargo test --lib`), and config.example.toml (generic template only) for src/config.rs changes. If the diff alters behaviour, a CLI command/flag, a config field, the data model, placement or GC, and does not update the owning doc, that is a finding. A hardcoded test count that no longer matches is a finding.

axes.name: DEPLOYMENT-CONFIG AND SECRET SAFETY
axes.detail: These are violations: adding or restoring a real config.deploy.toml or any instance config (real emails, bind addresses, TLS domains, quotas, host paths); committing a token, password or API key; hardcoding a secret instead of reading an env var; logging a token.

axes.name: ARCHITECTURE AND CORRECTNESS
axes.detail: Does the change respect the documented design (StorageBackend trait boundary, MVCC read/write/delete paths, multipart lifecycle, flat peak memory for multi-GB objects, GC and vacuum semantics)? Also flag clear correctness bugs in the diff, especially unsafe blocks, lock ordering, integer overflow in offset/length math, and error paths that silently succeed.

fail_guidance: Use 'fail' for genuine rule violations, a documented behaviour left stale with no doc edit, deployment-config/secret safety breaches, or real bugs. Use 'warn' for minor drift; 'pass' when there is nothing to report.
